title: Two Men Dived Nearly 7 Miles Down in 1960, and a Window Cracked

scenes.text: In 1960, two men sank nearly seven miles underwater.
Don Walsh and Jacques Piccard rode the bathyscaphe Trieste into the Challenger Deep.
The trip down took nearly five hours.
Somewhere on the way, a viewing port in the entry tube cracked.
They still reached the bottom, about 35,800 feet down, and stayed only minutes.
Then the sediment clouded the view, and they headed back up.

description:
In January 1960, Don Walsh and Jacques Piccard dived the bathyscaphe Trieste to the bottom of the Challenger Deep.
The descent took nearly five hours, a viewing port cracked, and they reached about 35,800 feet before sediment clouded the view and they surfaced.
Would you have gone down? Comment below.
first_comment: The crew heard the crack on the way down and kept going. Would you have turned back?
